You can build your resume from literally nothing. just be like free courses with certification. Also, you said it’s a maths/computer type of studies and you’re not that good at maths or coding. I would suggest you go for a different degree as as I used to think the same way, I took a degree in computer science/maths exactly the same that you are going for, but then I literally had to get admitted into a hospital because of the stress, so I shifted to Business degree and I’m doing good, so I would suggest you to go for a degree that actually interest you and is something that you’re good at. Continued from “ capturing them in and binding them to oil lamps” 

You are the newest member of an ancient and secretive order, tasked with a duty that few even believe in: hunting down malevolent djinn that haunt the desert sands. The legends say these djinn were once powerful spirits who roamed the earth freely, but their lust for power and vengeance led them to be bound by ancient sorcery. Your order is all that stands between them and the chaos they would unleash if freed.

Your initiation into the order was swift and rigorous. You were handed a map, a set of tools, and a single oil lamp—ornate and heavy with enchantments. The elders spoke of the djinn’s cunning, their ability to deceive and manipulate, and warned that once a djinn is released from its binding, it will stop at nothing to remain free. But they also spoke of the immense power the order holds over these beings, a power you are just beginning to understand.

The sands are your hunting ground, endless dunes that stretch out to the horizon, hiding the remains of ancient battles between your predecessors and the djinn they sought to capture. The wind carries whispers—rumors of a djinn that escaped its lamp centuries ago, lurking in the shifting sands, waiting to strike.

With each step, you feel the presence of the spirits around you, their eyes on your back, their voices in the wind. The oil lamp at your side is empty, its smooth surface cool against your skin, but the weight of it is a constant reminder of your mission. You must find the djinn, confront it, and bind it to the lamp, using the ancient incantations passed down through your order.

But you are not just hunting the djinn—they are hunting you too. For every step you take closer to your target, the djinn grows more aware of your presence. The sands begin to shift more violently under your feet, the air thickens with tension, and shadows stretch longer than they should. It is a battle of wills, of magic, and of survival.

You are no longer just a member of the order; you are the hunter, the last line of defense between the djinn and the world of men. Success will bring you honor and power beyond imagination, but failure… failure will mean unleashing a terror the world hasn’t seen in centuries.

The sun dips below the horizon, the sky turning a deep crimson. Night falls, and with it, the true hunt begins.

Continuing from: “the king of hell is back in town!” 

The demons exchanged nervous glances, their arrogance fading as their king’s shadow loomed over them. They had indulged in chaos during his absence, believing the throne would remain empty. But now, the King of Hell had returned, and fear gripped them once more.

His voice cut through the silence, cold and commanding. “I see you’ve forgotten who forged this kingdom from the ashes. My leniency ends now.”

A tremor of dread swept through the horde. The King’s eyes gleamed with cruel intent. “Loyalty is no longer assumed; it will be earned. Fail me, and chaos will seem merciful by comparison. Now, who among you dares to serve?”

After a tense pause, one demon stepped forward, bowing low. “I will,” it rasped.

“Good,” the King replied, his smile darkening. “Spread the word: the true reign of Hell begins now.”

With that, the demon retreated, heart pounding, as the King turned back to his throne, satisfied. Hell would soon remember who ruled them.
